_comment: English strings for planning mode (the site is English only); EVA mode (5-4) and the cuff checklist (5-5) add their own sections here. Keys starting with _ are notes, not shown.

ui.thinned: Table thinned to every n-th row for size; the chart uses all rows.

layers.comms_gaps: No line of sight to base (on routes)
layers.rudolph: Mount Sharp marker band & mantling unit (Rudolph et al.)
layers.b2_fallback: CTX (16 m) is shown underneath outside the HiRISE coverage.

info.P1: Routes built from Curiosity's actual drive path: shortest path on the track (loops and back-tracks removed), simplified with 5 m tolerance. Colour = slope class of each 2 m segment (larger 5 m slope of its two ends). Stations are the EVA reference points. Source: site/data/routes.json (scripts/40_route_profile.py).
info.P1c: Parts of each route not in direct line of sight from its base (2 m antenna, assumption). Viewshed on the 5 m DEM; no relays, no diffraction.
info.M1: MSL traverse (Vector/MSL_traverse), simplified with 1 m tolerance. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech.
info.M1w: 1,389 end-of-drive waypoints, sols 3–5073. Popups show the rover-recorded elevation and tilt, not DEM values.
info.M2: Four named investigation sites from the MSL traverse product.
info.M5: 237 raw Navcam/Mastcam images. Photos carry no geotag: each marker is the rover waypoint of that time, so the position is approximate.
info.M6: IAU-approved names from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (centre points only).
info.M7: Waypoint sol 3 (Bradbury Landing) and the latest waypoint in the data set.
info.T4: Contours every 50 m from the 10 m mean of the HiRISE DEM, simplified 10 m (positions within a few m). Elevations are DEM (areoid) values.
info.T4r: Contours every 10 m from the 5 m mean DEM around routes A and B, simplified 3 m.
info.G3: Line mapping of the marker band (confident / less confident / discontinuous / inferred), late mantling unit and high-albedo bench-forming unit on Aeolis Mons. Data: Mendeley Data mcdw3sp5vw v3 (Rudolph et al.). Unit and confidence come from the file names; nearest line is ~820 m from route B. Authors, licence and citation still to be confirmed before publishing.
info.G1: Global geologic map (Tanaka et al. 2014, USGS SIM 3292, 1:20,000,000). Clipped to a box around Gale, hence the straight edges. Context only.
info.E3: Dune fields and orbital hydrous/aqueous mineral detections (CRISM, OMEGA) from Mars Trek layers, clipped to Gale. Global surveys: few features inside Gale.
info.external: External tile server (NASA Mars Trek). Address scheme zoomOffset 0 (Plan/10). Needs network; the map's own tiles do not.
info.black_border: Black areas at the edge of the data are no-data; the layer is clipped to its bounds.

limits.B1: 16 m original, up to z11. The 5 m CTX mosaic failed the alignment check (strip offsets, median 283 m) and is not used (Plan/06).
limits.B2: Image covers 9 × 19 km along the traverse. z16 only in four rectangles around the traverse, z17 only around routes A and B.
limits.B4: 100 m grid. ~90 m mean, up to 270 m offset against the reference image (conditional pass, Plan/06). Brightness, not temperature.
limits.B5: 100 m grid. 43–229 m offset (conditional pass, Plan/06). Brightness, not temperature.
limits.T6: 463 m grid. ~300 m offset against the DEM (within one pixel).
limits.T1: Only inside the HiRISE DEM (36 × 40 km). DEM edges use lower-resolution fill (60–120 m position error possible).
limits.T2: 5 m grid slope; z14–15 enlarge the 5 m cells. On steep ground the 5 m slope reads lower than the rover tilt (Plan/10).
limits.T3: DEM elevation differs from rover-recorded elevation by up to ~20 m (DEM higher at higher elevation, Plan/06).
limits.T5A: Direct line of sight only (no diffraction, no relays). 5 m DEM. Base A = Bradbury Landing (assumed base).
limits.T5B: Direct line of sight only (no diffraction, no relays). 5 m DEM. Base B = rover waypoint sol 4614 (assumed base).
limits.E1: 100 m grid; 16–327 m offset after correction (conditional pass).

rad.title: Radiation (Curiosity RAD)
rad.period_recent: RAD sols {a}–{b} (2025), measured on route B
rad.period_early: RAD sols {a}–{b} (2012–13), measured at the route A site
rad.spike_day_E: Body, at the sol {sol} mean (transient event day)
rad.spike_route_note: The transient-event rows use the sol {sol} average rate for the whole EVA; the hour-by-hour replay of that day is part of EVA mode.
rad.no_spike_period: No sol in this period exceeds the transient-event threshold.
rad.year_equip: Equipment, one Earth year on the deck
rad.src_route: Absorbed dose = period mean rate × time (rad.json, period chosen by routes.json env.rad_period). Gy only; no equivalent dose (Sv).
rad.limits_short: Measured by RAD on the rover deck: not the dose inside a suit or an equipment box. No location dependence is claimed (RAD has no position data and the rover stayed within a few hundred metres). Route A and route B rates were measured 13 years apart (2012–13 and 2025). The difference between them must not be read as an effect of altitude or location; this data cannot separate the two.
rad.r1_title: Sol-mean dose rate, B and E
rad.r1_note: Design for the distribution, not only the mean: the daily mean changes from sol to sol. Dashed line = transient-event threshold for E (period mean + 3 SD).
rad.r2_text: Sol {sol} (UTC {utc}) is the only sol above the threshold: E sol mean {e} µGy/h ({pct}% above the period mean), largest single observation {max} µGy/h ({ratio}× the period mean). The rate rose for about 7 hours and fell back over 2–3 hours, then stayed slightly elevated for several sols.
rad.r2_cause: Labelled a transient event (unexplained rise). The cause has not been checked against solar-activity records, so it is not called a solar particle event here.
rad.threshold: threshold (period mean + 3 SD): E {e}, B {b} µGy/h
rad.r3_title: Mean dose rate by local time (LMST)
rad.r3_note: Highest vs lowest hour of E differ by {d}% — small compared with the transient event.
rad.r4_title: E dose rate vs REMS pressure (sol-hour means)
rad.r4_cap: RAD sols 4613–4843 × REMS same sol and LMST hour · {n} sol-hours
rad.r4_note: Weak negative correlation (more air above, slightly lower rate; about {slope}% per 100 Pa for E). Both quantities follow a daily cycle, so this is a correlation, not proof of shielding size.
rad.r4_src: Source: rad.json recent period ({n} valid RAD observations, sols 4613–4843) and REMS MODRDR pressure; {m} observations have a pressure value in the same sol and LMST hour.
rad.r4_recent_only: REMS pressure is paired with RAD only for sols 4613–4843.
rad.r5_title: Relative LET spectrum (B detector, summed over the period)
rad.r5_note: Shape only. RAD_RDR_SIS 4.2.1.6 describes the LET arrays as counts in bins of energy deposited in detector B, divided by the detector thickness (keV/µm); it gives no time normalisation for them. The values match counts divided by the live-time fraction of each observation; here they are summed over valid observations. No absolute flux and no SEE rate are derived. High-LET particles are rare but are the ones that can upset a memory cell.
rad.c_spike6: Body, 6 h at the sol {sol} mean
rad.c_src: rad.json conversion block: body 6 h {e6} µGy, equipment 6 h {b6} µGy(Si), year {y} mGy(Si). 1 Gy = 100 rad.
rad.lens_tid: Detector B is silicon, so its absorbed dose is the quantity used for total ionizing dose (TID). At this period's mean, a part exposed on the deck for one Earth year collects about {mgy} mGy = {y} rad(Si). Part TID ratings are given on datasheets in krad(Si); compare with the rating of the specific part. This page quotes no typical rating because it has no citable source for one.
rad.lens_see: Single-event effects are caused by one energetic particle, not by accumulated dose. Whether a given part is affected depends on its sensitive volume and LET threshold, which this data does not contain. The LET distribution (R5) shows that high-LET particles are present; no rate is computed.
rad.lens_transient_text: On sol {sol} the single-observation peak was {ratio}× the period mean. For electronics the concern is the higher particle flux during such an event (more chances of single-event effects), not the small extra total dose.
rad.lens_transient_none: No transient event above the threshold in this period's data.
limits: RAD sits on the rover deck; dose inside a suit, a vehicle or an equipment box depends on shielding.
Absorbed dose (Gy) only. Equivalent dose (Sv) and health limits are not computed.
No spatial map and no altitude dependence: RAD files carry no rover position and the rover moved only a few hundred metres in each period.
Route A and route B rates were measured 13 years apart (2012–13 and 2025). The difference between them must not be read as an effect of altitude or location; this data cannot separate the two.
Periods are short slices of a Mars year (669 sols) and of the ~11-year solar cycle.
Observations whose QC flag is not 00000000 are excluded. RAD_RDR_SIS 4.2.1.2 defines 00000001 as 'unknown quality control issues may exist'.

temp.title: Weather and ground temperature (Curiosity REMS)
temp.n_sols: {n} sols with data, {f} with ≥20 h covered, {rows} rows
temp.surface_note: Ground temperature = REMS infrared ground-temperature sensor, hourly means. It is the environment an exposed surface sees, not the temperature inside a suit or an equipment box (which have heat capacity and heaters).
temp.diurnal_title_route: Ground temperature by local time, Ls {ls}–{ls2}°
temp.cap: REMS sols {a}–{b}, {n} sols in this season, hourly means
temp.cap_full: REMS sols {a}–{b}, {n} sols with ≥20 h covered
temp.cap_all: REMS sols {a}–{b}, mean over all sols
temp.h1_note: This season: coldest hour {min}, warmest {max}, swing {r} K; {n40} of {nv} hours below −40 °C, {n55} below −55 °C.
temp.air_note: Minima are read from ground temperature: the air-temperature series has an implausible low hourly mean ({amin} K) that is treated as a sensor outlier.
temp.h2_title: Daily ground-temperature swing (max − min of hourly means)
temp.h2_note: One thermal cycle per sol, 669 per Mars year. Larger swings fatigue solder joints and packages faster.
temp.h3_title: Mean hour-to-hour change of ground temperature
temp.h3_note: Fastest warming {up} K/h (starting {hu} h), fastest cooling {down} K/h (starting {hd} h): after sunrise and before sunset.
temp.h4_title: Hours per sol with ground temperature below −40 °C / −55 °C
temp.h4_note: −40 °C and −55 °C are reference lines for comparison. Without heating, an exposed surface spends more than half of each sol below −40 °C.
temp.h5_title: Daily coldest and warmest hour vs season (Ls)
temp.h6_title: Daily swing distribution, share of sols
temp.h6_cap: Sols 1–360 ({na} sols) vs sols 4134–4843 ({nb} sols), ≥20 h covered
temp.h6_note: Different places and different years; sols 1–360 cover about half a Mars year, so compare like seasons (H5) before drawing conclusions.
temp.h7_title: THEMIS thermal inertia along the routes
temp.h7_cap: THEMIS TI 100 m (alignment-corrected) at route samples
temp.h7_note: Mean thermal inertia: route A {a} TIU, route B {b} TIU. Mean daily swing: sols 1–360 {ra} K, sols 4134–4843 {rb} K. Lower thermal inertia (sand, dust) gives larger day–night swings; the two periods also differ in season and year, so this is a direction, not a fit.
temp.lens_cycle: an exposed surface goes through one cycle per sol with a mean swing of {r} K (up to {rmax} K), heating at up to {up} K/h after sunrise and cooling at {down} K/h before sunset. Repeated swings fatigue solder joints and packages; enclosures and heaters reduce what the electronics actually see.
temp.lens_cold: On average {h} hours per sol are below −40 °C at the surface, so unheated exposed equipment would spend most nights below that reference line.
temp.lens_ref_lines: The −40 °C / −55 °C lines are comparison references only; this page does not state part temperature grades because it has no citable source for them.
limits: Ground temperature is not suit or equipment-internal temperature.
Hourly means; sols with fewer than 20 covered hours are excluded from swing statistics.
Route B period ground-temperature uncertainty is about 9 K (route A about 2 K).
Wind is not shown: no usable wind rows in sols 4134–4843.
Empty hours in a season curve are left as gaps here; EVA mode interpolates and marks them.

about.title: About this map
about.home_link: Home: project overview, EVA replay and cuff checklist
about.intro: A planning tool for a walking EVA (extravehicular activity) in Gale Crater, Mars. Two routes follow ground Curiosity actually drove: route A on the flat crater floor near the landing site, route B up the lower slope of Mount Sharp. Radiation and temperature come from Curiosity's RAD and REMS instruments, measured at those same places.
source_list: MRO: HiRISE colour mosaic (0.25 m) and HiRISE DEM (1 m) → slope, hillshade, elevation, line of sight; CTX mosaic (16 m).
MSL Curiosity: traverse and waypoints (with recorded tilt), RAD dose rates (PDS RDR), REMS ground temperature and pressure (PDS MODRDR), Navcam/Mastcam raw images.
Mars Odyssey: THEMIS night and day infrared, THEMIS thermal inertia.
Geology: Rudolph et al. marker band / mantling mapping (Mendeley Data), USGS SIM 3292 global map; place names from the USGS Gazetteer.
about.not_done: What this map does not do
not_done_list: No radiation map or altitude dependence; no equivalent dose (Sv); no single-event-effect rates.
No suit or equipment-internal temperatures; ground temperature only.
No wind (no usable wind data in the route B period).
No live position or forecast; values are past measurements.
key_list: Tab moves through the layer list, map and panels; the map pans with the arrow keys and zooms with + / −.
Panel tabs: Left / Right arrows switch tabs.

dose.def: Energy that radiation leaves in 1 kg of material. 1 Gy = 1 J/kg; the old unit rad is 0.01 Gy.

dose_rate.def: Absorbed dose per hour. RAD reports µGy/h; dose rate × exposure time = cumulative dose.

B.def: RAD's silicon detector: the dose silicon (electronics) receives.

E.def: RAD's plastic scintillator; used here as the body-side reading.

GCR.def: High-energy particles from outside the solar system; the steady main part of radiation at the Martian surface.

SPE.def: A burst of particles from a solar eruption that raises dose rates for hours to days.

TID.def: Dose a part accumulates over its life. It shifts transistor thresholds and raises leakage; ratings are given in krad(Si).

SEE.def: An error caused by a single energetic particle crossing a chip, e.g. a memory bit flip (SEU) or latch-up (SEL). A matter of probability, not accumulation.

LET.def: Energy a particle leaves per µm of material (keV/µm). Higher LET makes a single-hit error more likely.

QC.def: 8-character quality flag on each RAD observation. RAD_RDR_SIS 4.2.1.2 defines 00000000 as no issue and 00000001 as 'unknown quality control issues may exist'.

LMST.def: Local mean solar time on Mars: the sol divided into 24 'hours' at that place.

sol.def: A Mars day, about 24 h 40 min. 'Sol 4843' is the 4843rd Mars day after Curiosity landed.

Ls.def: Mars' position in its year, 0–360°; one Mars year is about 669 sols.

cycle.def: Daily rise and fall of temperature. Materials expand differently, so solder joints and packages fatigue.

TI.def: How well the surface stores heat. Low (sand, dust) → large day–night swing; high (rock) → small swing.

DEM.def: Digital elevation model: a grid whose values are elevations (m).

slope.def: Ground inclination (°) from elevation differences between neighbouring DEM cells.

hillshade.def: The DEM lit by a virtual sun so relief looks three-dimensional.

viewshed.def: Area visible in a straight line from a point without terrain in the way; used as an approximation of radio coverage from the base.

tilt.def: Angle of the rover body from horizontal; close to a measurement of the local ground slope.

waypoint.def: Where the rover ended a drive; has sol, position, elevation and tilt.

RAD.def: Curiosity's Radiation Assessment Detector: the long-term record of radiation at the Martian surface.

REMS.def: Curiosity's weather station: air and ground temperature, pressure, UV.

HiRISE.def: MRO cameras: HiRISE high-resolution (0.25 m, stereo DEMs), CTX wide-area (~5 m) greyscale.

THEMIS.def: THEMIS: Mars Odyssey infrared camera. MOLA: MGS laser altimeter.

EVA.def: Extravehicular activity: here, walking outside the base in a suit.

draw.title: Draw your own route (P3)
draw.intro: Draw a line on the map. Length, climb, slope classes, walking time and an elevation profile are computed from the 10 m grid. The grid (about 5 MB) is loaded the first time you use this tool.
draw.how_mouse: Mouse: press "Draw line", click to add points, double-click (or "Finish") to end. "Undo point" removes the last point.
draw.how_touch: Touch: tap to add points. Use the buttons on the map for Undo and Finish. Drag to pan, pinch to zoom.
draw.how_key: Keyboard: focus the map (Tab), move it with the arrow keys so the cross-hair is where you want a point, then Enter adds a point, Backspace undoes, F or Esc finishes, Delete clears.
draw.empty: No line yet. Press "Draw line" on the map and click two or more points.
draw.need_two: One point so far. Add at least one more.
draw.error: The 10 m grid could not be loaded. The drawn length is still shown on the map toolbar.
draw.approx_detail: Slopes on a 10 m grid are measured at a different scale than the 5 m / 2 m values of routes A and B, so slope classes, climb and walking time can come out a little different (longer or shorter) than in the route panel. Elevation is the DEM value, not a measured rover height.
draw.outside_warn: {len} m ({pct} %) of the line is outside the 10 m grid. For that part only the length is counted: no elevation, slope or time is given.
draw.all_outside: The whole line is outside the 10 m grid, so only its length is given. No elevation, slope or time is computed.
draw.impassable_warn: {len} m has a slope of {deg}° or more (impassable by the walking rule). The time below covers only the rest.
draw.rt_note: twice one way; stay time not included
draw.profile_title: Elevation profile of the drawn line
draw.profile_cap: 10 m grid, sampled every 5 m along the line · bands: orange = slope 15° or more, purple = outside the grid
draw.src: Source: 10 m grid made from the HiRISE DEM (Plan/10 sec.1). Speed rule: the same as the route panel (flat speed, slope factors in "Assumptions").
